scope: Pure Source chain and negative fixtures. No Canon, Native, Go, SQLite, Main23 child or model execution.

findings.observation: validate_root_capture accepts when each expected SHA appears anywhere in JSON-serialized output. It does not require the expected path and bytes or a typed ref to be present, nor correlate output content with the claimed operation.
findings.reproduction: A 3-row session/call/output fixture whose output contains only three digests, no ref paths or sizes, returns True. This same validator gates the review witness, postreview live capture and activation capture.
findings.required_change: Parse the actual tool result as a typed evidence object; bind each complete exact path/sha256/bytes ref and operation/call context, and use the raw tool timestamps rather than only self-declared binding timestamps. Reject digest-only output.

findings.observation: runtime_closure checks independent_non_author and review_author strings copied across qualification and decision files but does not bind that decision to an actual external reviewer capture or reviewer-authored manifest. Both are inputs to the Root request.
findings.reproduction: A pure fixture with an invented non-author reviewer string and matching resource_refs is accepted by runtime_closure. File I/O was replaced only to isolate the decision predicate; this is a Source-logic reproduction, not a live filesystem exploit.
findings.required_change: Require a pinned, reviewer-authored decision/HDF/MF and an external Root hostpair witnessing those exact refs before any registration or build phase uses the qualified runtime closure.

positive_controls: Author HDF, MF and all 12 manifest members match their actual pinned bytes.
The source calls for fresh post-public371 Canon refs and a separate output root.
The review did not start the builder or modify Canon.
